history.heading: Before colonisation
paragraphs: The Central African Republic lies at the heart of the continent, between the savannas of the Sahel and the Congo rainforest. Its peoples include Banda, Gbaya, Sara, Mandja and the Aka forest people. From the 16th to 19th centuries, slave raids by sultanates to the north and by traders linked to the Atlantic and trans-Saharan trade devastated the region.

history.heading: French colony
paragraphs: France colonised the area in the 1880s and 1890s, naming it Ubangi-Shari. Concession companies used forced labour to collect rubber and ivory, causing great suffering. The territory became part of French Equatorial Africa. Barthélemy Boganda led the movement for independence but died in a plane crash in 1959.

history.heading: Independence and instability
paragraphs: The country became independent on 13 August 1960. In 1966 Jean-Bédel Bokassa seized power; he proclaimed himself emperor in 1976 in a lavish coronation and was overthrown with French help in 1979. Coups, mutinies and rebellions continued for decades.

In 2013 the mainly Muslim Séléka rebel coalition took power, provoking the rise of mainly Christian anti-balaka militias and sectarian violence that killed thousands and displaced a large part of the population. A UN peacekeeping mission has been deployed since 2014, and since 2018 the government has relied on Russian security forces, including the Wagner Group.

culture.heading: Peoples and traditions
paragraphs: The country has dozens of ethnic groups, but Sango is spoken by almost everyone as a national language, alongside French. Most people are Christian, with a Muslim minority, and traditional beliefs remain influential.
The polyphonic singing of the Aka Pygmies is recognised by UNESCO. Food is based on cassava, often eaten as a dough with sauces of greens, peanuts or meat.

politics.heading: Fragile state
paragraphs: The Central African Republic is a presidential republic, but the state controls limited territory, and armed groups operate in much of the country. A 2023 constitutional referendum removed presidential term limits, allowing President Faustin-Archange Touadéra to run for a third term.
The government relies on Russian security support and UN peacekeepers, and peace agreements with armed groups have often broken down.

economy.heading: Rich resources, deep poverty
paragraphs: Despite deposits of diamonds, gold, uranium and timber, the Central African Republic is one of the poorest countries in the world, with very low life expectancy and widespread food insecurity. Most people live from subsistence agriculture.

Insecurity, poor infrastructure and corruption have prevented development, and much mining is informal or controlled by armed groups or foreign companies. The currency is the Central African CFA franc. In 2022 it briefly made Bitcoin legal tender, a decision later reversed.
